authenticity.method: every contract whose name ends in "Robinhood Token" in the chain explorer was tested on chain: (1) decimals() is 18 and uiMultiplier() answers — 202 of 286 passed; (2) keccak256(eth_getCode) equals one reference bytecode hash — 194 of the 202 passed; (3) as an independent cross-check, the creator of each of the 202 was looked up in the explorer: all 194 share one creator address and the 8 rejected do not. Tests 2 and 3 agree on every contract. The 194 carry 194 distinct symbols

reproducibility.bytecode: anyone can re-run it over any RPC at the latest block, any time after the snapshot: eth_getCode at the address, keccak256 of the answer, compare with codeHash
reproducibility.creator: taken from the contract-creator field of the chain explorer on the snapshot date; scripts/rebuild-registry.mjs --rebuild re-reads it from the explorer API

authenticity.period: snapshot taken 2026-09-20; the issuer adds Stock Tokens over time, so the list is a snapshot while the rule is not
authenticity.source: Robinhood Chain state via eth_getCode / eth_call, plus contract creators from the chain explorer
authenticity.caution: a token with a matching symbol but a different contract address is not a Robinhood Stock Token — the registry is keyed by ADDRESS, never by symbol

multiplier.what: the ERC-8056 corporate-action multiplier: Stock Tokens never rebase, so dividends and splits are expressed as this number instead. 1.0 means no corporate action has been applied yet
multiplier.scale: 1e18 = 1.0, a constant of the specification — uiMultiplierDecimals() does not exist on chain (the call reverts on every token)
multiplier.method: one eth_call to uiMultiplier() per token, batched 8 per request, read at the latest block
multiplier.period: live value at the moment of the read; no history is collected, because a backward log scan would exceed what the public node allows

sharePrice.what: the price of ONE underlying share, derived from the price of a whole Stock Token
sharePrice.method: share price = token price ÷ uiMultiplier. DIVISION, not multiplication: an oracle or a pool prices a WHOLE token and the multiplier is already inside that price, so applying it again would count the dividend twice
sharePrice.source: this package does not price tokens; bring a token price (for example a Chainlink feed on this chain) and divide it by the multiplier above

data.rights: Stock Token data here is chain state read over a third-party public RPC and served for verification and display only, not for resale (resaleOk: false on this answer). Read the terms of service of Robinhood Chain (https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/terms-of-service) before reusing this data
